summary: Josephine County lookout on Kerby Peak, in use from at least 1916; the L-4 cab burned or was removed in 1959, and a climbing guide reports remnants on the summit.

facts.status_note: Lookout gone after 1959 (burned, per newspaper items and SummitPost; removed or destroyed, per the register and firelookout.com); SummitPost reports a few remnants of the structure on the summit

access.note: SummitPost describes a route from Selma on Highway 199 to a trailhead with parking for at least five vehicles, no Northwest Forest Pass required; not accessible in winter and spring

visit.trail_note: Gravel road to a trailhead, then a hike to the summit; SummitPost says the mountain is not accessible in winter and spring

events.note: Lookout station located on Kerby Mountain and a telephone line built to the summit, per 1916 newspaper items
Lookout discovered and reported a small fire near Love Station
W. M. Barr sent to the lookout station; a 1923 item has William Barr there, and says he came home when the season closed
Ben Carlyle named as the lookout man for the season
Lightning badly damaged the lookout house; repairs made by men sent from Grants Pass
Elevated L-4 cab per FFLOS and firelookout.com. Newspaper items show a lookout station by 1916 and a state-built house by 1928, so the cab may have replaced an earlier house; no source says so
State fire warden hurt in a fall from a cliff in the Kerby region was taken to the lookout station and carried out by a patrol of 12 men
May 1958 item: the old lookout would be rebuilt, or possibly moved to Roundtop. No source says either happened
Burned, because the building was feared to be infected with tuberculosis (newspaper compilation); SummitPost says it burned down

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com give 1934 for the L-4 cab. Newspaper items show a lookout station from 1916 and a state-built house by 1928. Recorded the 1934 cab as the built event and kept the earlier items as separate events; the sources do not say whether the cab replaced an earlier house.
The register says removed in 1959 and firelookout.com says destroyed. Newspaper items and SummitPost say it burned in 1959. The story says it burned and notes the register's wording.

notes_for_editor: Brief record was right on status (gone), elevation (1,693 m / 5,555 ft, not in facts) and registration (2011). The 1934 build date conflicts with the 1916 and 1928 newspaper references. Ben Bleecha is spelled Bleecha in 1957 and Blecha in 1958. The register's 'removed' and firelookout's 'destroyed' differ from the 'burned' in newspaper items. The newspaper items are only as reliable as the Oregon Lookouts compilation; originals were not checked. SummitPost is a climbing site, so its access note is not an agency statement. No source describes the summit in 2026.
